1	# Meridian — Chrome Web Store submission copy
2	
3	Last updated: July 26, 2026
4	
5	Publisher-facing copy for the Chrome Web Store listing, the **Privacy
6	practices** tab, and the per-permission justification fields. It is derived from
7	the source in this repository (manifest, `background.js`, `utils/`, and
8	`components/`) and reconciled with `docs/privacy-meridian.md` and `README.md`.
9	
10	> **Owner action required.** Everything here is draft copy for review. It is not
11	> a submission and does not certify anything in the Chrome Web Store dashboard.
12	> Paste each block into the matching dashboard field, confirm it against the
13	> exact archive you upload, and complete the owner-only follow-ups at the end of
14	> this document. Items marked **[OWNER-ONLY — NOT DONE]** were not and cannot be
15	> performed from the repository.
16	
17	---
18	
19	## 1. Store listing
20	
21	### Name
22	Meridian
23	
24	### Summary (short description, ≤132 characters)
25	Spatial tab command center — a visual new-tab page that turns your open tabs
26	into searchable thumbnail cards.
27	
28	### Category (suggested)
29	Workflow & Planning (or Productivity)
30	
31	### Detailed description
32	Meridian replaces your new-tab page with a spatial command center for your open
33	tabs.
34	
35	Your tabs appear as live thumbnail cards, organized into workspace lanes that
36	map to Chrome tab groups or to custom groups you create in Meridian. Drag to
37	reorder tabs within and across groups, collapse lanes you are not using, and
38	hover a card to open a full-size preview with the tab's title and URL.
39	
40	**Features**
41	- **Tab cards & workspace lanes** — every open tab as a live thumbnail, grouped
42	  into collapsible lanes with drag-and-drop reordering.
43	- **Local search** — instantly find open tabs by title, URL, domain, and page
44	  context. Bookmark and history search are optional and off until you turn them
45	  on.
46	- **Multi-engine web search** — search with Google, DuckDuckGo, Bing, or Brave
47	  from the top of every new-tab page; your choice is remembered.
48	- **Theming & backgrounds** — Light, Dark, or System theme; solid colors,
49	  gradient presets, curated Picsum photos, or your own uploaded image.
50	- **Tab organization** — optionally cluster ungrouped tabs by domain.
51	- **Flexible new-tab behavior** — open a fresh Meridian view, return to a pinned
52	  Meridian tab, or load a custom homepage.
53	- **Keyboard-first** — jump to Meridian, move between tabs and lanes, focus
54	  search, and create groups without the mouse.
55	
56	**Privacy**
57	Meridian runs entirely in your browser. It has no accounts, no analytics, and no
58	Meridian-operated server. Your tab, page, screenshot, bookmark, and history data
59	stays in your Chrome profile. Full details are in the extension's privacy policy.
60	
61	---
62	
63	## 2. Privacy practices tab
64	
65	### 2.1 Single purpose (single-purpose description field)
66	Meridian is a new-tab replacement that helps users view, search, and organize
67	their open browser tabs as a visual, spatial workspace. Every permission and
68	data access exists to render tabs as searchable thumbnail cards, to search local
69	browser data the user opts into, and to personalize the new-tab surface.
70	
71	### 2.2 Data types collected or used
72	Declare the following categories in the dashboard. All are used **on-device for
73	the extension's features**; none are transferred to a Meridian-operated server.
74	
75	| Dashboard data type | Applies? | What it covers in Meridian |
76	| --- | --- | --- |
77	| **Web browsing activity** | Yes | Open tab titles, URLs, domains, tab-group membership, window IDs, tab activation/previous-tab state, and — only if the user enables them — bookmark and browsing-history entries used for local search. |
78	| **Website content** | Yes | Per-tab meta-description and H1/H2 heading text read after a page finishes loading, and JPEG screenshots of the visible area of active tabs captured for thumbnails/previews. Screenshots can contain whatever is on screen at capture time. |
79	| **User activity** | Yes (recommended) | Tab activation, previous-tab tracking, grouping, ordering, and workspace assignments that drive the UI. Disclosed here because reviewers may treat this interaction/usage state as user-activity data. |
80	| Personally identifiable information | No | Not collected. |
81	| Health information | No | Not collected. |
82	| Financial and payment information | No | Not collected. |
83	| Authentication information | No | Not collected. |
84	| Personal communications | No | Not collected. |
85	| Location | No | Not collected. |
86	
87	> The user's **uploaded custom background image** and **preferences** (theme,
88	> background choice, search provider, enabled local-search sources, new-tab
89	> behavior, optional homepage URL, domain-grouping) are user-provided content
90	> stored on the device. Preferences sync through the user's own Chrome Sync if
91	> enabled; the uploaded image bytes and captured screenshots are never placed in
92	> sync storage. Map these to the dashboard's user-content categories as the
93	> current form requires.
94	
95	### 2.3 Data usage certifications
96	Based on the reviewed source, the publisher should be able to affirm all three
97	required certifications — **confirm each against the uploaded archive before
98	checking the box:**
99	
100	- ☑ I do **not** sell or transfer user data to third parties outside of the
101	  approved use cases.
102	- ☑ I do **not** use or transfer user data for purposes unrelated to my item's
103	  single purpose.
104	- ☑ I do **not** use or transfer user data to determine creditworthiness or for
105	  lending purposes.
106	
107	### 2.4 Privacy policy URL
108	`https://emberstone-studio.com/docs/privacy/meridian`
109	
110	Meridian-specific policy text lives in `docs/privacy-meridian.md` in this
111	repository. **[OWNER ACTION STILL NEEDED]** Publish that content at the URL
112	above before entering it in the dashboard, then confirm the live page matches
113	`docs/privacy-meridian.md`.
114	
115	---
116	
117	## 3. Data handling disclosure (paste-ready listing block)
118	
119	Meridian processes the following **locally in your browser** to provide its
120	features. Most of it stays in on-device storage; preferences are the exception
121	and can sync through your own Chrome Sync account (see "Local & sync storage"
122	below):
123	
124	- **Browsing activity** — open tab titles, URLs, domains, tab-group membership,
125	  and tab activation/order, used to display, search, and manage your tabs. A
126	  local search index and workspace/UI state are stored in `chrome.storage.local`.
127	- **Website content** — after a page loads, Meridian reads its meta description
128	  and H1/H2 headings so local search can match page context beyond the title and
129	  URL. It does not read form input or other page-body text.
130	- **Screenshots** — Meridian captures the visible area of active tabs after tab
131	  activation or page load, and during a user-requested full refresh that cycles
132	  eligible tabs. Automatic captures (activation/page load) do not filter by URL
133	  in Meridian's code — Chrome's `captureVisibleTab` API itself refuses
134	  `chrome://`, Chrome Web Store, and other extensions' pages, so only those
135	  attempts fail; any other page, including one with sensitive content on
136	  screen, is captured. The full refresh additionally skips `chrome://`,
137	  `chrome-extension://`, and `about:` tabs in Meridian's own code before
138	  switching to them. Screenshots are stored as JPEG blobs in extension-local
139	  IndexedDB; cache metadata and refresh markers use `chrome.storage.local`.
140	  Storage targets roughly 200 entries / ~50 MB and
141	  prunes the oldest thumbnails first, but a still-open tab's thumbnail is never
142	  evicted to make room, so usage can exceed that target while those tabs stay
143	  open. A tab's thumbnail is removed when the tab closes.
144	- **Local & sync storage** — preferences (theme, background, search provider,
145	  enabled local-search sources, new-tab behavior, optional homepage, domain
146	  grouping) are stored in `chrome.storage.sync`. If the user has Chrome Sync
147	  turned on, Chrome syncs this data through the user's own Google/Chrome
148	  account to their other signed-in devices, subject to the user's Chrome Sync
149	  settings — it is not Meridian-operated syncing. Workspaces, search metadata,
150	  thumbnails, the Meridian/previous tab IDs, and an uploaded custom background
151	  image stay in `chrome.storage.local` / IndexedDB and are not synced.
152	- **Optional bookmarks & history** — off by default. Meridian requests bookmark
153	  or history access only when you enable that source in Settings → Local Search
154	  or select its search scope, and queries it only to show local-search results.
155	  It keeps no separate persistent copy; revoking access turns the source off.
156	- **External requests** — search-provider icons load from fixed Google,
157	  DuckDuckGo, Bing, and Brave icon URLs (these contain no visited URL); favicons
158	  resolve through Chrome's packaged `_favicon` provider (not Google S2); the
159	  background settings load photo previews and selected photos from
160	  `picsum.photos` by seed. Starting a web search, opening a result, or choosing a
161	  custom homepage navigates your browser to that destination normally.
162	- **Retention & deletion** — data persists in local/sync storage until replaced,
163	  evicted, cleared, or removed with the extension or profile. Closing a tab
164	  deletes its cached thumbnail and search entry (including extracted metadata).
165	  You can clear all extension data through Chrome's controls.
166	- **Outbound links in Settings** — the Settings panel's Emberstone Studio
167	  footer contains two static links: the studio site
168	  (`https://emberstone-studio.com`) and a Ko-fi donation page
169	  (`https://ko-fi.com/emberstonestudio`). They do nothing until the user
170	  explicitly clicks one, which opens that destination in a new tab. Meridian
171	  makes no background request for them and adds no click tracking or analytics.
172	- **No telemetry or backend** — Meridian has no Meridian-operated server, no
173	  analytics or advertising SDK, no account system, and no telemetry uploader.
174	
175	---
176	
177	## 4. Permission justifications
178	
179	Paste each string into the matching "why do you need this permission?" field.
180	
181	### Required permissions
182	
183	**`tabs`**
184	Read tab titles, URLs, domains, and group/window membership and act on tabs
185	(activate, close, move, group, restore) so Meridian can render the new-tab page's
186	tab cards, power local tab search, and manage tabs from its UI.
187	
188	**`tabGroups`**
189	Read and manage Chrome tab groups so Meridian's workspace lanes reflect and can
190	modify tab-group membership and grouping.
191	
192	**`storage`**
193	Persist the user's preferences, workspaces, tab-search index (including extracted
194	page metadata), thumbnail cache metadata, and tab-tracking state in
195	`chrome.storage.local`/`chrome.storage.sync`, plus JPEG thumbnail blobs in
196	IndexedDB, so settings and layout survive across sessions.
197	
198	**`unlimitedStorage`**
199	Screenshot thumbnails are stored as JPEG blobs in IndexedDB and can exceed the
200	default storage quota. `unlimitedStorage` lets the local thumbnail cache hold enough
201	entries to be useful. Code targets roughly 200 entries / ~50 MB and prunes the
202	oldest thumbnails first when over that target, but never evicts a thumbnail for
203	a tab that is still open — so actual usage can exceed the target while those
204	tabs stay open.
205	
206	**`favicon`**
207	Display site icons for tabs and search results by resolving page URLs through
208	Chrome's packaged `_favicon` provider, avoiding third-party favicon lookups.
209	
210	**`sidePanel`**
211	Provide Meridian's side-panel UI, which opens when the toolbar icon is clicked.
212	
213	**`scripting`**
214	After an open tab finishes loading, run a one-shot extractor that reads only that
215	page's meta description and H1/H2 heading text into the local tab-search index,
216	so local search can match page context beyond the title and URL. It does not read
217	form input or other page-body content. `scripting` (rather than click-scoped
218	`activeTab`) is required because this indexing happens automatically on page
219	load, not from a user click.
220	
221	**`host_permissions: <all_urls>`**
222	Allow two automatic, non-click actions across the tabs the user already has open:
223	(1) capturing the visible tab via `captureVisibleTab` after tab activation, after
224	a page finishes loading, and during a user-requested full refresh, to build
225	thumbnail cards; and (2) running the load-time meta/H1/H2 metadata extractor
226	above. Chrome's click-scoped `activeTab` cannot authorize these automatic
227	background actions, so broad host access is required for the shipped
228	live-thumbnail and auto-indexing behavior. Neither automatic action filters by
229	URL in Meridian's own code; Chrome's `captureVisibleTab` and `scripting` APIs
230	refuse to act on `chrome://`, Chrome Web Store, and other extensions' pages, so
231	those are excluded by Chrome's own restrictions, not by a Meridian allowlist.
232	The separate, user-requested full refresh does explicitly skip `chrome://`,
233	`chrome-extension://`, and `about:` tabs in Meridian's code before switching to
234	them. Meridian makes no network request to a Meridian server.
235	
236	### Optional permissions (requested only on demand)
237	
238	**`bookmarks`** *(optional)*
239	Requested only when the user enables bookmark search in Settings → Local Search
240	or selects the bookmark scope. Used to read bookmark titles, URLs, and folder
241	names to return local-search results. No persistent copy of the bookmark tree is
242	created; denying or revoking it leaves the feature off.

**PASTE VERBATIM — plain text, no Markdown:**

```
Meridian replaces your new-tab page with a spatial command center for your open tabs.

Your tabs appear as live thumbnail cards, organized into workspace lanes that map to Chrome tab groups or to custom groups you create in Meridian. Drag to reorder tabs within and across groups, collapse lanes you are not using, and hover a card to open a full-size preview with the tab's title and URL.

• Tab cards and workspace lanes — every open tab as a live thumbnail, grouped into collapsible lanes with drag-and-drop reordering.
• Local search — instantly find open tabs by title, URL, domain, and page context.
• Side panel — open Meridian's search from Chrome's side panel with the toolbar icon, without leaving the page you are on.
```

Meridian is a new-tab replacement that helps users view, search, and organize

# SECTION 5 — Permission justifications (dashboard only, never public)

Paste each string into the matching "why do you need this permission?" field.
These are read by reviewers, not by users.

### Required permissions

**`tabs`**
Read tab titles, URLs, domains, and group/window membership and act on tabs
(activate, close, move, group, restore) so Meridian can render the new-tab page's
tab cards, power local tab search, and manage tabs from its UI.

**`tabGroups`**
Read and manage Chrome tab groups so Meridian's workspace lanes reflect and can
modify tab-group membership and grouping.

**`storage`**
Persist the user's preferences, workspaces, tab-search index (including extracted
page metadata), thumbnail cache metadata, and tab-tracking state in
`chrome.storage.local`/`chrome.storage.sync`, plus JPEG thumbnail blobs in
IndexedDB, so settings and layout survive across sessions.

**`unlimitedStorage`**
Screenshot thumbnails are stored as JPEG blobs in IndexedDB and can exceed the
default storage quota. `unlimitedStorage` lets the local thumbnail cache hold enough
entries to be useful. Code targets roughly 200 entries / ~50 MB and prunes the
oldest thumbnails first when over that target, but never evicts a thumbnail for
a tab that is still open — so actual usage can exceed the target while those
tabs stay open.

**`favicon`**
Display site icons for tabs and search results by resolving page URLs through
Chrome's packaged `_favicon` provider, avoiding third-party favicon lookups.

**`sidePanel`**
Provide Meridian's side-panel UI, which opens when the toolbar icon is clicked.

**`scripting`**
After an open tab finishes loading, run a one-shot extractor that reads only that
page's meta description and H1/H2 heading text into the local tab-search index,
so local search can match page context beyond the title and URL. It does not read
form input or other page-body content. `scripting` (rather than click-scoped
`activeTab`) is required because this indexing happens automatically on page
load, not from a user click.

**`host_permissions: <all_urls>`**
Allow two automatic, non-click actions across the tabs the user already has open:
(1) capturing the visible tab via `captureVisibleTab` after tab activation, after
a page finishes loading, and during a user-requested full refresh, to build
thumbnail cards; and (2) running the load-time meta/H1/H2 metadata extractor
above. Chrome's click-scoped `activeTab` cannot authorize these automatic
background actions, so broad host access is required for the shipped
live-thumbnail and auto-indexing behavior. Neither automatic action filters by
URL in Meridian's own code; Chrome's `captureVisibleTab` and `scripting` APIs
refuse to act on `chrome://`, Chrome Web Store, and other extensions' pages, so
those are excluded by Chrome's own restrictions, not by a Meridian allowlist.
The separate, user-requested full refresh does explicitly skip `chrome://`,
`chrome-extension://`, and `about:` tabs in Meridian's code before switching to
them. Meridian makes no network request to a Meridian server.

**`bookmarks`** *(optional)*
Requested only when the user enables bookmark search in Settings → Local Search
or selects the bookmark scope. Used to read bookmark titles, URLs, and folder
names to return local-search results. No persistent copy of the bookmark tree is
created; denying or revoking it leaves the feature off.

**`history`** *(optional)*
Requested only when the user enables history search in Settings → Local Search or
selects the history scope. Used to read history titles, URLs, and visit times to
return local-search results. No persistent history database is created; denying
or revoking it leaves the feature off.

# SECTION 7 — Reference: data-handling detail (NOT a store field)

**This is not pasted anywhere in the listing.** The public Privacy tab is
generated from §3's structured input only. The text below is the source material
for the **privacy policy page** at the §3.4 URL, and the reference used to answer
reviewer questions. It is kept here because it is the most precise description of
runtime behavior in the repository.

- **Browsing activity** — open tab titles, URLs, domains, tab-group membership,
  and tab activation/order, used to display, search, and manage your tabs. A
  local search index and workspace/UI state are stored in `chrome.storage.local`.
- **Website content** — after a page loads, Meridian reads its meta description
  and H1/H2 headings so local search can match page context beyond the title and
  URL. It does not read form input or other page-body text.
- **Screenshots** — Meridian captures the visible area of active tabs after tab
  activation or page load, and during a user-requested full refresh that cycles
  eligible tabs. Automatic captures (activation/page load) do not filter by URL
  in Meridian's code — Chrome's `captureVisibleTab` API itself refuses
  `chrome://`, Chrome Web Store, and other extensions' pages, so only those
  attempts fail; any other page, including one with sensitive content on
  screen, is captured. The full refresh additionally skips `chrome://`,
  `chrome-extension://`, and `about:` tabs in Meridian's own code before
  switching to them. Screenshots are stored as JPEG blobs in extension-local
  IndexedDB; cache metadata and refresh markers use `chrome.storage.local`.
  Storage targets roughly 200 entries / ~50 MB and prunes the oldest thumbnails
  first, but a still-open tab's thumbnail is never evicted to make room, so
  usage can exceed that target while those tabs stay open. A tab's thumbnail is
  removed when the tab closes.
- **Local & sync storage** — preferences (theme, background, search provider,
  enabled local-search sources, new-tab behavior, optional homepage, domain
  grouping) are stored in `chrome.storage.sync`. If the user has Chrome Sync
  turned on, Chrome syncs this data through the user's own Google/Chrome
  account to their other signed-in devices, subject to the user's Chrome Sync
  settings — it is not Meridian-operated syncing. Workspaces, search metadata,
  thumbnails, the Meridian/previous tab IDs, and an uploaded custom background
  image stay in `chrome.storage.local` / IndexedDB and are not synced.

  or history access only when you enable that source in Settings → Local Search
  or select its search scope, and queries it only to show local-search results.
  It keeps no separate persistent copy; revoking access turns the source off.

  DuckDuckGo, Bing, and Brave icon URLs (these contain no visited URL); favicons
  resolve through Chrome's packaged `_favicon` provider (not Google S2); the
  background settings load photo previews and selected photos from

  font request leaves the browser. Starting a web search, opening a result, or
  choosing a custom homepage navigates your browser to that destination

- **Retention & deletion** — data persists in local/sync storage until replaced,
  evicted, cleared, or removed with the extension or profile. Closing a tab
  deletes its cached thumbnail and search entry (including extracted metadata).
  You can clear all extension data through Chrome's controls.

  explicitly clicks one, which opens that destination in a new tab. Meridian
  makes no background request for them and adds no click tracking or analytics.
- **No telemetry or backend** — Meridian has no Meridian-operated server, no
  analytics or advertising SDK, no account system, and no telemetry uploader.

---

  and "optional bookmarks/history" are used consistently in `README.md`,

"

```
• Tab cards and workspace lanes — every open tab as a live thumbnail, grouped into collapsible lanes with drag-and-drop reordering.
• Local search — instantly find open tabs by title, URL, domain, and page context.
• Side panel — open Meridian's search from Chrome's side panel with the toolbar icon, without leaving the page you are on.
• Bookmarks and history panel — reach bookmarks and recent history from a dropdown in the top bar, with site icons and one-click open. Both sources are optional and stay off until you turn them on.
• Multi-engine web search — search with Google, DuckDuckGo, Bing, or Brave from the top of every new-tab page; your choice is remembered.
• Theming and backgrounds — Light, Dark, or System theme; solid colors, gradient presets, curated photos, or your own uploaded image.
• Tab organization — optionally cluster ungrouped tabs by domain.
• Flexible new-tab behavior — open a fresh Meridian view, return to a pinned Meridian tab, or load a custom homepage.
• Keyboard-first — jump to Meridian, move between tabs and lanes, focus search, and create groups without the mouse.

PRIVACY

Meridian runs entirely in your browser. It has no accounts, no analytics, and no Meridian-operated server. Your tab, page, screenshot, bookmark, and history data stays in your Chrome profile. Full details are in the extension's privacy policy.
```

# Privacy tab

## Single purpose
Meridian is a new-tab replacement that helps users view, search, and organize
their open browser tabs as a visual, spatial workspace. Every permission and
data access exists to render tabs as searchable thumbnail cards, to search local
browser data the user opts into, and to personalize the new-tab surface.

## Data types — check these three
- **Web browsing activity** — tab titles, URLs, domains, group membership,
  activation state; plus bookmarks/history only if the user enables them.
- **Website content** — meta description and H1/H2 text read after page load,
  and JPEG screenshots of active tabs for thumbnails.
- **User activity** — tab activation, grouping, ordering, workspace assignments.

Everything else (PII, health, financial, authentication, communications,
location) is **No**.

## Certifications — check all three
Confirm against the uploaded archive first.

- ☑ Not sold to third parties outside approved use cases.
- ☑ Not used or transferred for purposes unrelated to the single purpose.
- ☑ Not used to determine creditworthiness or for lending.

---

# Permission justifications

**`tabs`**
Read tab titles, URLs, domains, and group/window membership and act on tabs
(activate, close, move, group, restore) so Meridian can render the new-tab page's
tab cards, power local tab search, and manage tabs from its UI.

**`tabGroups`**
Read and manage Chrome tab groups so Meridian's workspace lanes reflect and can
modify tab-group membership and grouping.

**`storage`**
Persist the user's preferences, workspaces, tab-search index (including extracted
page metadata), thumbnail cache metadata, and tab-tracking state in
`chrome.storage.local`/`chrome.storage.sync`, plus JPEG thumbnail blobs in
IndexedDB, so settings and layout survive across sessions.

**`unlimitedStorage`**
Screenshot thumbnails are stored as JPEG blobs in IndexedDB and can exceed the
default storage quota. `unlimitedStorage` lets the local thumbnail cache hold
enough entries to be useful. Code targets roughly 200 entries / ~50 MB and prunes
the oldest thumbnails first when over that target, but never evicts a thumbnail
for a tab that is still open — so actual usage can exceed the target while those
tabs stay open.

**`favicon`**
Display site icons for tabs and search results by resolving page URLs through
Chrome's packaged `_favicon` provider, avoiding third-party favicon lookups.

**`sidePanel`**
Provide Meridian's side-panel UI, which opens when the toolbar icon is clicked.

**`scripting`**
After an open tab finishes loading, run a one-shot extractor that reads only that
page's meta description and H1/H2 heading text into the local tab-search index,
so local search can match page context beyond the title and URL. It does not read
form input or other page-body content. `scripting` (rather than click-scoped
`activeTab`) is required because this indexing happens automatically on page
load, not from a user click.

**`host_permissions: <all_urls>`**
Allow two automatic, non-click actions across the tabs the user already has open:
(1) capturing the visible tab via `captureVisibleTab` after tab activation, after
a page finishes loading, and during a user-requested full refresh, to build
thumbnail cards; and (2) running the load-time meta/H1/H2 metadata extractor
above. Chrome's click-scoped `activeTab` cannot authorize these automatic
background actions, so broad host access is required for the shipped
live-thumbnail and auto-indexing behavior. Neither automatic action filters by
URL in Meridian's own code; Chrome's `captureVisibleTab` and `scripting` APIs
refuse to act on `chrome://`, Chrome Web Store, and other extensions' pages, so
those are excluded by Chrome's own restrictions, not by a Meridian allowlist.
The separate, user-requested full refresh does explicitly skip `chrome://`,
`chrome-extension://`, and `about:` tabs in Meridian's code before switching to
them. Meridian makes no network request to a Meridian server.

**`bookmarks`** *(optional)*
Requested only when the user enables bookmark search in Settings → Local Search
or selects the bookmark scope. Used to read bookmark titles, URLs, and folder
names to return local-search results. No persistent copy of the bookmark tree is
created; denying or revoking it leaves the feature off.

**`history`** *(optional)*
Requested only when the user enables history search in Settings → Local Search or
selects the history scope. Used to read history titles, URLs, and visit times to
return local-search results. No persistent history database is created; denying
or revoking it leaves the feature off.

Only the whitespace step failed — tests, syntax, and manifest parsing all passed. Let me reproduce it and see whether it's only `.tasker/`.

`.gitignore:1` flagged for "trailing whitespace" on `+.claude/` — that's a `\r`. The CRLF conversion is wider than the files I normalized; I only fixed ones whose diff was CRLF-*only*.

Some of those are binaries (woff2/png) that merely contain the byte pair — I must not touch those. Let me check whether there's genuine trailing whitespace beyond the `\r`.

Clear picture: **0** source files have genuine trailing whitespace — it's all `\r`. Only 4 `.tasker/` files have real trailing spaces, and those are server-owned transcripts that get rewritten. Two fixes needed.

Parity and tests hold. But there's a consequence I need to handle: the index is now LF while the worktree still has CRLF, so the ZIP I built — and its recorded tree hash — no longer match what a fresh clone would produce.

Committing the line-ending fix and repackage.

Normalize line endings to LF and scope the whitespace check

The release-checks whitespace step failed on main. `git diff --check` reported
tens of thousands of "trailing whitespace" errors, but no source file actually
had a trailing space — an editor had saved files as CRLF, and the CR is
reported as trailing whitespace on every line of every converted file.

- Add .gitattributes with `* text=auto eol=lf` so the repository stores LF
  regardless of the editor that writes a file, with binary formats (png, webp,
  woff2, zip, ai) explicitly excluded — several contain CR LF inside compressed
  data and would be corrupted by conversion.
- Renormalize the tracked tree, and normalize the 15 worktree files that were
  still CRLF so the working copy matches what a fresh clone produces.
- Exclude `.tasker/` from the whitespace check. It holds machine-written board
  state and agent transcripts that embed captured command text with genuine
  trailing spaces, and the Tasker server rewrites them, so the repository
  cannot durably keep them clean. Four such files were the only genuine
  trailing whitespace anywhere in the repo.

Repackage as a result: normalizing line endings changes file bytes, so the
previously recorded candidate tree hash no longer described what a clean
checkout would produce. Rebuilt and re-verified the archive, and updated the
release record with the new tree hash, archive name, size, and digest.

     Render with: inkscape -w N -h N img/icon-source.svg -o img/iconN.png

     Ink counter, not a knockout. These PNGs are composited over backgrounds we
     cannot predict: the extensions page, the Web Store grid, the puzzle-piece
     overflow menu, in either theme. A knocked-out M is a transparent hole, so
     on a light backdrop it becomes light-on-mint at 1.67:1 and the letterform
     disappears. Filling the counter with the brand ink puts the M at 7.95:1

     rasterised in an image context where prefers-color-scheme and CSS mask are
     not dependably honoured, and the failure mode is silent. Chrome does not
     show a broken icon, it quietly keeps the previously cached one, which looks
     exactly like the new artwork never shipped.

          node-version: "24"

        run: node --test tests/*.test.mjs

      - name: Check runtime JavaScript syntax
        shell: bash
        run: |
          while IFS= read -r -d '' file; do
            echo "Checking $file"
            if ! node --check "$file"; then
              echo "::error file=$file::JavaScript syntax check failed"
              exit 1
            fi
          done < <(git ls-files -z -- '*.js')

      - name: Parse extension manifests

          const { readFileSync } = require("node:fs");

              console.error(
                `::error file=${file}::Manifest JSON parse failed: ${error.message}`,
              );
              process.exitCode = 1;

      # `.tasker/` is excluded from every invocation below. It holds machine-written
      # Tasker board state and agent transcripts, which embed captured command text
      # with real trailing spaces and are rewritten by the Tasker server — so the
      # repository cannot durably keep them clean, and failing the build on them
      # says nothing about the extension. This check exists to police hand-written
      # source; .gitattributes keeps that source LF-normalized.
      - name: Check committed changes for whitespace errors
        shell: bash
        env:
          EVENT_NAME: ${{ github.event_name }}
          PR_BASE_SHA: ${{ github.event.pull_request.base.sha }}
          PR_HEAD_SHA: ${{ github.event.pull_request.head.sha }}
          PUSH_BEFORE_SHA: ${{ github.event.before }}
          PUSH_AFTER_SHA: ${{ github.event.after }}
          DEFAULT_BRANCH: ${{ github.event.repository.default_branch }}
        run: |
          zero_sha=0000000000000000000000000000000000000000

          case "$EVENT_NAME" in
            pull_request)
              echo "Checking pull request changes: $PR_BASE_SHA...$PR_HEAD_SHA"
              git diff --check "$PR_BASE_SHA...$PR_HEAD_SHA" -- . ':!.tasker'
              ;;
            push)
              if [[ "$PUSH_AFTER_SHA" == "$zero_sha" ]]; then
                echo "Branch deletion has no new content to check."
                exit 0
              fi

              before="$PUSH_BEFORE_SHA"
              if [[ "$before" == "$zero_sha" ]]; then
                default_branch="origin/$DEFAULT_BRANCH"
                echo "Checking new branch changes: $default_branch...$PUSH_AFTER_SHA"
                git diff --check "$default_branch...$PUSH_AFTER_SHA" -- . ':!.tasker'
                exit 0
              fi

              echo "Checking pushed changes: $before..$PUSH_AFTER_SHA"
              git diff --check "$before" "$PUSH_AFTER_SHA" -- . ':!.tasker'
              ;;
            workflow_dispatch)
              echo "Checking the latest commit at HEAD."
              git diff --check HEAD^ HEAD -- . ':!.tasker'
              ;;
          esac

# Normalize line endings to LF in the repository, regardless of the editor or
# platform that wrote the file. Without this, an editor saving CRLF rewrites
# every line of a file, which buries real changes in whitespace churn and trips
# the `git diff --check` step in .github/workflows/release-checks.yml — the CR
# is reported as trailing whitespace on every line.
* text=auto eol=lf

# Binary formats must never be line-ending converted. Several of these legitimately
# contain the CR LF byte pair inside compressed data, and "normalizing" it corrupts
# the file.
*.png   binary
*.webp  binary
*.woff2 binary
*.zip   binary
*.ai    binary
